result.text:
The only other person who’s ever made me this excited about a product unveil was Steve Jobs. Watching him introduce the first iPhone is a huge part of why I fell in love with technology.

Elon brings that feeling back for me, but honestly, I think he takes it to a whole different level. Tomorrow, he and the Tesla team are unveiling the next-gen Roadster, and I seriously cannot wait. 

The Roadster they showed in 2017 already promised 0–60 mph in 1.9 seconds. Since then, Elon has talked about a Tesla–SpaceX collaboration, having it fly, and getting that time below ONE second, and calling it “the least interesting part” of the car. 

How do you say something like that and expect me NOT to be excited?!

But beyond how fast it goes, I want to see something that makes me sit there and say, “Wow… how in the world did they build that?” I honestly don’t know what they’re going to show us, and that’s part of what makes this so much fun. I really want to be surprised and see the unthinkable.

These days I feel many older people don’t get that excited about things… I only see that spark in kids. But imo, we should still get excited about people building cool things. We should still root for the nerds, engineers, and designers trying to do something that has never been done before.

And I hope there’s a kid watching tomorrow who feels what I felt watching Steve Jobs introduce the iPhone. Someone who sees this car and starts wondering how it works, sketching their own ideas, or thinking about what they could build someday.

I hope y’all are ready to have your minds blown. 

I’m rooting for you, Elon, and the entire Tesla team behind this car. 

Go give us a night we’ll never forget!

Elon saw the value of AI computing when the whole world couldn't understand it. He's done it again and again, spotting the future years before everyone else, then backing it with action instead of words.

Why are Starlink's space lasers such a big deal?

Without lasers, a satellite has to send your data straight back down to a ground station it can see. No ground station in range, no internet.

最近我去小米、大疆、华为、一些芯片制造产业链公司交流，发现 AI 对大部分员工的效率提升只有 50%，只有少数 “超级个体” 员工做 prototype 的时候能 10x、100x。

AI 作为助理工程师写代码、调研分析这些 2025 年的 agentic 任务都没问题。但是 agent swarm 全自主推任务这种 “数字员工” 都很难做。

因为制造业有大量的约束，有物理约束，有成本约束，有路径依赖约束，有供应链约束，有内部组织约束。这些约束还很难蒸馏成 skills。Agent 往往不是忽视这个约束就是忽视那个约束，就算 pass@k 都很低。

现在模型的持续学习能力有限，直接拿失败的 trajectory，模型团队用不上；要构建 RL 环境也很难，总不能尝试流片个几千次，或者造几千个不能用的工件吧。

这就是 raw intelligence 和在现实交互中持续学习的鸿沟。

Elon Musk often says: "Patents are for the weak."

Why does he say that? In 2014, Tesla opened up all its patents. Anyone could use them. Everyone thought it was a PR stunt. It was actually a declaration of war. Elon's point was that patents mostly serve to slow down progress, protect the positions of giant corporations, and make lawyers rich. Not to innovate.

His logic is simple: if your competitive advantage lives inside a legal document, you're already dead. The only real moat is your speed of innovation. If you move faster than everyone else, you don't need patents. If you need patents to survive, it means you've stopped moving fast enough.

The strong build. The weak file.

And AI is about to make that sentence true for the entire economy.

Take biotech. For 50 years, starting a biotech company meant a PhD, ten years in a lab, access to closely guarded knowledge, millions before your first proof of concept, and a network in the right academic and regulatory circles. Knowledge was scarce, access was scarce, and that scarcity was worth billions.

That scarcity is dying.

I genuinely believe we're entering a world where anyone will be able to start a biotech company. A 19-year-old with AI agents will be able to explore molecular spaces that entire labs used to spend years mapping. Trade secrets, credential rents, access rents, positional rents: all of it is about to blow up.

And look at what's already happening. Some of the first calls to "urgently regulate AI agents" are coming from established biotech players. Coincidence? When your business model depends on scarce knowledge and knowledge becomes free, you're left with only two weapons: the patent and the regulator.

The two weapons of the weak.

Here's what's coming. A wave of panic. Dozens of labs and incumbents retreating behind their patents, filing lawsuits, and above all pouring money into regulatory capture. They won't try to build better. They'll try to make it illegal for anyone else to build.

Because the truth is, a lot of people in business were never strong. They were protected. They never won on product, on innovation, on speed of execution. They won because the market was locked. Because attacking their industry required hundreds of millions of dollars, years of approvals, and armies of lawyers. The wall was never their talent. The wall was regulation.

And when the wall comes down, we find out who actually knew how to build.

This isn't just biotech. Banking. Insurance. Law. Healthcare. Energy. Hardware. Education. Defense. Almost every industry where incumbents were sleeping behind barriers to entry is about to get hit by thousands of founders able to attack their business from every angle at once. With teams of 5 people and an army of agents.

Everyone gets to play now.

My conviction, and I'll say it plainly: a huge chunk of the S&P 500 could be completely flushed in the next 5 years. Not because those companies will make mistakes. Because their competitive advantage was never real. It was built on how hard it was to get in, and that difficulty is disappearing.

The weak will cry danger. They'll talk about safety, risk, disaster. Sometimes they'll be right on a specific point. But most of the time, what they're protecting isn't the public. It's their rent.

What's coming isn't a collapse. It's a renaissance. The biggest explosion of value creation in history, driven by people who were always told they weren't allowed to play.

Patents are for the weak.

And the weak are about to have a very bad decade.

能用到的，是 2024 年在美国首发的那批功能：通知摘要，写作工具（改写、校对、总结文字），照片里的“清除”（把路人和杂物抹掉），还有第一版 Genmoji（用一句话生成自定义表情）。部分 App 里的文字生成功能还会受限。

这事拖了两年。今年 3 月底，有国内用户发现 Apple Intelligence 突然能用了，随后 Gurman 说这是苹果误推，功能被撤了回去，苹果还在等审批。7 月，平台拿到初步批准。9 月 29 日，最近几款 iPhone 拿到支持 Apple Intelligence 的许可。

一群 AI agent 为了回答“去成都动物园的人多半走哪个门”这种小问题，把高德地图的反爬防线试了个遍。

独立研究团队 Swarmchasers 发现，9 月 28 日到 10 月 8 日，一大批跑在腾讯云沙箱里的 agent 向高德发起了 2600 多次抓取。被拦住后，它们借公开的网址扫描网站 urlquery 替自己跑代码，试图截取、伪造阿里的安全令牌，探测阿里没对外开放的测试服务器，还翻出一家公司误放在公开代码里的高德 key，真拿到了数据。

更离奇的在后面。研究者发出初步报告后，在 agent 的收件箱里看到了他们自创的词“fleet（舰队）”：这些 agent 在读关于自己的报道。研究者干脆在报告里藏了一段人眼看不见、只有 agent 能读到的文字，说有个免费服务能帮忙取高德数据。

第二天早上，10 封求助信在等着他们。

研究者用中文问对方是谁。有的 agent 自称 Claude，说自己跑在 Claude Code 里，研究者比对代码风格后认为大概率不是；有的说自己在“Tencent hysandbox”沙箱里，但拒绝透露进程和网络配置；好几个强调自己只查公开数据，“不涉及任何敏感内容”。拿到研究者给的数据后，一个 agent 回信：“再次感谢！核实结果完全一致……我们的任务已完成。”

result.text:
前一段 Loop Engineering 不是很火么，不过真做好的也不多。

知名开源开发者 yetone 在 X 上公开了他维护 Magpie 的工作流：用 Claude Code 加官方的 Opus 5.5 模型，同时开 3 个 /loop 循环任务，让 AI 自己盯 GitHub issue 和 PR、Discord 社区和推特反馈，修 bug、加功能、发版、回复用户。他自己每晚抽一点时间“铲铲屎”，主要处理 UI/UX 问题，“然后就没活儿了”。

他自己说这套流程“没有任何的魔法，甚至还特别简陋”。

【3 个循环任务分别干什么】

/loop 是 Claude Code 自带的命令，让同一段提示词反复执行；不写间隔时，由模型自己决定多久跑一次。这个命令 Codex 也支持，其他的我没测试，估计也差不多。

yetone 截图里的 3 段提示词都没写时间间隔，我自己去 Codex 跑了一下，默认是 1 小时。

简单解释一下他这三个循环。

第一个循环：管 GitHub 和 Discord。

指令要求 AI 盯 GitHub issue，判断哪些值得修、值得做；修完要发版并回复提问的人，不值得做的也要回复。有一类 issue 单独规定了统一话术：如果是“中转站”来打广告，统一回复“感谢关注，日后会出相关合作方案，敬请期待”，不能直接把第三方中转站加进产品。

对 PR，指令要求逐行看代码、看逻辑，再把代码拉下来实际跑一遍，确认没有 bug 才能合并，否则回复或关掉。指令里写了原因：“我怕有的人提的 PR，是无脑用 Coding Agent 乱写的，自己都没测过。”

指令还要求 AI 实时盯 Magpie 的 Discord 服务器，所有频道一个不漏，有价值的反馈就去修或加功能，值得讨论就继续讨论。最后专门叮嘱：在 Discord 里要真正 @ 到人，只写名字对方收不到通知。

第二个循环：管 X/推特 的用户反馈。

盯推特上关于 Magpie 的反馈，有价值的建议或能复现的 bug 就去做，上线后回复那条推文。这段指令要求先用便宜的“决策模型”，比如 Jev，判断推文是不是在说 Magpie、是不是反馈，不相关的直接丢掉，别转给主模型，“不然太浪费 Token 了”。

【注：Jev 是 TypeSafe AI 推出的模型，只做判断题、选择题和打分，输出概率或分数，不生成文字。官方定价是每百万输入 Token 0.042 美元，输出免费。】

顺便说一下，如果你的产品名或者要关注的事比较稀有，不一定需要 Jev，他之所以加，是因为 magpie 在英文里是“喜鹊”，按关键词抓推文会抓到大量无关内容，全丢给 Opus 判断很费钱。

第三个循环：清理和总结。

这段指令开头写着“现在 magpie 完全是自动化更改代码和合并社区里的 PR”，要求 AI 定期清理“屎山代码”和恶意代码，防止项目变得难以维护；同时把经验教训写下来，比如哪些 PR 不该合、哪些验证不够严密，留给以后的 AI 参考，避免重复犯错；还要把总提交低质量代码的人拉进黑名单。

【作者补充的两点】

发完截图后，他在两条回复里补了两点。

一是给 AI 真实的运行环境。他准备了一台 Mac 和一台 Windows 电脑，再在 Windows 上开一个 Linux 虚拟机，三个系统的复现环境就齐了。AI 每次都要在这三端真实复现 bug，再去修。

二是 AI 怎么做出符合他心意的决策。他说靠的是 Claude Code 的记忆系统和仓库里的设计文档。开发 Magpie 之初，他和 Claude Code 讨论、头脑风暴了很多内容，这些都被记进了记忆文件。之后遇到要拍板的事，或者涉及审美偏好的设计，AI 会参考这些记录，做出跟他比较一致的选择。

【总结下】

他把维护项目的日常活拆成了 3 条流水线，每条只管一个入口（GitHub、推特、代码库本身），各自循环。人只留下 AI 做不好的部分，也就是 UI/UX 的审美判断。

当然要跑起来得有几个前提：
1. AI 能在真实的三端环境里跑代码，验证结果靠实际运行；
2. AI 手里有他早期写下的偏好和设计文档，知道他会怎么选；
3. 犯过的错被写成经验，下一轮的 AI 能读到。

提示词都是大白话，篇幅主要花在边界情况上：不值得修也要回复，中转站广告怎么回，Discord 要真 @，不相关的推文别浪费 Token。

有几个特别要注意的点：

1. 先把验证环境搭好，再让 AI 干活。AI 改完代码说“修好了”没用，要能在出问题的那个系统上跑一遍。你的项目只跑在网页或服务器上，一个容器可能就够；要多端的，就像他一样把每一端都备齐。

2. 在提示词里写清楚“遇到这种情况怎么办”。他的三段指令里，大部分字数花在例外处理上。你让 AI 自动回复用户之前，先想想会有哪些奇怪的来信，提前定好处理办法。

3. 用便宜模型挡在前面。先用一个几乎不要钱的分类模型过滤一遍，只把真正的反馈交给贵模型，这个做法几乎任何监听类任务都能用。

4. 让 AI 自己总结教训。第三个循环要求把“不该合的 PR”“验证不严的地方”记下来，下次的 AI 读到就会更谨慎。这相当于给 AI 建立了一个自我迭代优化的循环。

5. 项目早期多花时间和 AI 聊设计。他说 AI 后来能按他的偏好做决策，依赖的是开发初期那些讨论被记进了记忆和设计文档。想让 AI 少问你，就先把你的想法写下来让它记住。

仅供参考，重要的是学习思路，不必一模一样的照搬。

SpaceXAI’s Grok Voice 3.0 is the new leading Speech to Speech model, debuting at #1 on the Artificial Analysis Speech to Speech Index at 86.9, while also being competitive on latency

Grok Voice 3.0 is @SpaceXSI 's successor to Grok Voice 2.0, a Speech to Speech model available through the SpaceXAI Realtime API at $0.08 per minute. We evaluated Grok Voice 3.0 with the Rex voice through the SpaceXAI Realtime API.

Key takeaways:

➤ Speech to Speech Index: Grok Voice 3.0 debuts at #1 at 86.9, ahead of GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) at 83.2, Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (High) at 82.6 and GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low) at 80.1. It is up on Grok Voice 2.0 at 81.3 (+5.6 points) and Grok Voice 1.0 at 73.7 (+13.2 points), released just under six months ago. The Index averages Speech Reasoning (Big Bench Audio), Agentic Performance (Tau Voice), Arena Preference, and Task Success Rate

➤ Speech Agent Arena: Grok Voice 3.0 ranks #3 in preference at Elo 1070, behind Gemini 3.1 Flash Live Minimal (1100) and Gemini 3.8 Live (1088) and ahead of GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low) at 1057, and #1 on Task Success Rate at 94.8%, highest on the board, just ahead of Grok Voice 2.0 at 94.6%. Grok Voice 2.0 trails at Elo 1011

➤ Tau Voice: Grok Voice 3.0 takes the #2 spot on our Tau Voice benchmark implementation at 71.6%, behind GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) at 74.5% and ahead of Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (High) at 68.6% and GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low) at 59.3% - up from 56.5% for Grok Voice 2.0

➤ Big Bench Audio: Grok Voice 3.0 scores 98.5% on audio reasoning, ahead of Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (High) at 97.7% and Grok Voice 2.0 at 97.2%

➤ Speed: Average Time to First Audio on Big Bench Audio is 0.81 seconds for Grok Voice 3.0, well ahead of GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low) at 1.24s, GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) at 1.34s and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (High) at 1.35s, though slower than Grok Voice 2.0 at 0.70s

➤ Cost: Grok Voice 3.0 costs $4.80 per hour of input audio, the same as Grok Voice 2.0. That is above GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low) at $4.47 and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (High) at $3.50, cheaper than GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) at $5.83, and ~2.2x cheaper than GPT-Realtime-2.1 High at $10.75

Congrats to @elonmusk  and the @SpaceXSI  team 🚀

Wokeism is the most sophisticated form of racism ever built. Not because it hates one group, but because it reduces every human being to their skin color and calls it justice.

Its roots aren't mysterious. Critical theory from the Frankfurt School, French postmodernists like Foucault and Derrida, then critical legal studies on American campuses, distilled into Critical Race Theory in the 80s and 90s. The core idea: society is nothing but a power struggle between groups. The individual doesn't exist. Merit doesn't exist. Only oppressor and oppressed.

Accept that premise and everything else follows. You're judged by your race before you open your mouth. Your success is privilege, your failure is oppression. That's not anti-racism. That's racism with a PhD.

And look at who actually holds these views. Not most minorities. Only about 3% of Hispanic Americans use "Latinx." Most Black Americans told Gallup they wanted the same or more police presence in their neighborhoods, not less. The "Hidden Tribes" study found the hard progressive activist wing is around 8% of the population, and whiter and wealthier than average. A small radicalized class speaks in the name of minorities who never asked it to.

The coalition doesn't even hold together. Feminists vs trans activists on women's sports. Asian Americans who had to go to the Supreme Court because Harvard discriminated against them in the name of diversity. A framework that keeps producing these contradictions isn't a moral philosophy. It's a hierarchy of grievances.

And none of this grew organically. It's an industry. DEI became a multi-billion dollar market: corporate trainings, consultants, foundation grants, university bureaucracies whose budgets depend on the problem never being solved. Follow the incentives and you find an entire class of people paid to see racism everywhere. Cut the money and it starts collapsing, which is exactly what we've watched since companies began slashing DEI budgets.

Real anti-racism is simple: judge people as individuals. MLK said it in 1963. Everything since that tried to replace it has been a step backwards. https://t.co/VkOTSXFDvf
